content: 1. Ruxolitinib topical levels or effects may be increased by quinine due to its impact on hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown but considered minor. Close monitoring is advised. 2. Sarecycline can elevate quinine levels or effects by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Exercise caution and monitor for potential toxicities of P-gp substrates, which may necessitate dosage adjustments when co-administered with P-gp inhibitors. Close monitoring is recommended. 3. Sarilumab may reverse the inhibitory effects of elevated IL-6 on CYP450 enzyme activity, potentially restoring CYP activity and decreasing drug concentrations. Caution is advised when initiating or discontinuing sarilumab in patients on CYP450 substrates, particularly those with a narrow therapeutic index. Close monitoring is required. 4. Schisandra may increase quinine levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Secukinumab may normalize CYP450 enzyme formation altered by chronic inflammation and elevated cytokines. When initiating or discontinuing secukinumab in patients on CYP450 substrates, especially those with a narrow therapeutic index, monitor therapeutic effects closely. 6. Selexipag levels or effects may be increased by quinine due to reduced metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Reduce the selexipag dose to once daily if co-administered with moderate CYP2C8 inhibitors. 7. Selpercatinib may increase quinine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Sertraline and quinine both prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of cardiac arrhythmias. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Sevoflurane and quinine both prolong the QTc interval, posing a serious risk. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 10. Quinine may increase siponimod levels or effects by affecting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Co-administration with moderate CYP2C9 and moderate/strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is not recommended. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, necessitating avoidance or alternative therapy. 11. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride increases quinine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and consider preand post-colonoscopy ECGs in patients at risk of serious cardiac arrhythmias. 12. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate increases quinine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and consider ECG monitoring in high-risk patients. 13. Solifenacin and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Somapacitan decreases quinine levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Limited data suggest growth hormone treatment increases CYP450-mediated clearance. 15. Somatrogon decreases quinine levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Growth hormone treatment may increase CYP450-mediated clearance. 16. Somatropin decreases quinine levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Growth hormone treatment may enhance CYP450-mediated clearance. 17. Sorafenib and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Sotalol and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Sotorasib decreases quinine levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, refer to the prescribing information for dosage modifications. 20. St. John’s Wort decreases quinine levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Stiripentol increases quinine levels or effects by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Stiripentol is a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer, requiring monitoring of co-administered CYP3A4 substrates for altered effects. 22. Quinine enhances succinylcholine effects through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. This combination is contraindicated. 23. Sulfamethoxazole increases quinine levels or effects by competing for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance is unknown but considered minor. Monitor closely. 24. Sunitinib and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Tacrolimus and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Quinine increases talazoparib levels or effects by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Talazoparib is a P-gp substrate, and co-administration with P-gp inhibitors may increase systemic exposure. 27. Talquetamab increases quinine levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Talquetamab may suppress CYP enzyme activity due to cytokine release syndrome (CRS), increasing CYP substrate exposure. 28. Quinine increases tamsulosin levels by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Tazemetostat decreases quinine levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, while quinine increases tazemetostat levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Teclistamab increases quinine levels or effects by altering metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Teclistamab may suppress CYP450 enzyme activity due to cytokine release, increasing CYP substrate exposure. 31. Tecovirimat decreases quinine levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Tecovirimat is a weak CYP3A4 inducer. 32. Telavancin and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Telotristat ethyl decreases quinine levels or effects by inducing CYP3A4. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Monitor for suboptimal efficacy and consider increasing the dose of the CYP3A4 substrate. 34. Tepotinib increases quinine levels or effects by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the P-gp substrate dosage as recommended. 35. Tetrabenazine and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 36. Tetracaine and quinine may cause methemoglobinemia when co-administered. Monitor for signs of methemoglobinemia. 37. Thioridazine and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. 38. Thiothixene and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Quinine increases tinidazole levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Tipranavir increases quinine levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 41. Tobramycin inhaled and quinine both increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Avoid concurrent or sequential use to reduce ototoxicity risk. 42. Topiramate decreases quinine levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown but considered minor. 43. Quinine increases topotecan levels or effects by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Oral topotecan product labeling recommends avoiding P-gp inhibitors. 44. Toremifene and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Quinine increases triamterene levels or effects by competing for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance is unknown but considered minor. 46. Triclabendazole and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Quinine increases trimethoprim levels or effects by competing for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance is unknown but considered minor. 48. Trimipramine and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Trofinetide increases quinine levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Monitor CYP3A4 substrates for potential toxicities when co-administered with trofinetide. 50. Tucatinib increases quinine levels or effects by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the CYP3A substrate dose as per product labeling. 51. Turmeric increases quinine levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Quinine increases toxicity of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Exercise extreme caution when co-administering vilanterol with QTc-prolonging drugs. 53. Ustekinumab may normalize CYP450 enzyme formation altered by chronic inflammation. When initiating or discontinuing ustekinumab in patients on CYP450 substrates, particularly those with a narrow therapeutic index, monitor therapeutic effects closely. 54. Quinine and vandetanib both prolong the QTc interval, increasing toxicity. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, frequent ECG monitoring is recommended. 55. Vardenafil and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Quinine enhances vecuronium effects through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing the risk of respiratory depression. This combination is contraindicated. 57. Vemurafenib and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 58. Quinine increases venetoclax levels or effects by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If a P-gp inhibitor must be used, reduce the venetoclax dose by at least 50% and monitor for toxicities. 59. Verapamil increases quinine levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, while quinine increases verapamil levels by competing for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance is unknown but considered minor. 60. Quinine increases toxicity of vilanterol/fluticasone furoate inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Exercise extreme caution when co-administering vilanterol with QTc-prolonging drugs. 61. Viloxazine increases quinine levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Viloxazine may increase systemic exposure of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. 62. Voclosporin and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 63. Vonoprazan increases quinine levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Vonoprazan is a weak CYP3A inhibitor.
